text: Seabrook Town made a super comeback and won 4-2 against Harbour City. Harbour City scored first with goals by Elias Okafor and Marek Barros[#905][#975]. But Seabrook Town didn't give up! When they changed their plan, they pressed harder and played faster[#1361]. Then Tariq Marlowe scored to start the comeback[#1104]. At the very end, Kian Romano scored two quick goals and won the game for his team[#1882][#1906]. While playing wide and crossing often, Seabrook Town’s smart moves and lots of teamwork helped them win[#1361]. Imagine a speedy dolphin swimming past defenders to score two big goals—that’s how Kian Romano helped his team win[#1882].

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for kid audience in en

- Seabrook Town won with a final score of 4-2 despite being down 2-0 early in the match [#905, #975, #1104].
- Marek Barros scored for Harbour City with an xG of 0.185 and assisted Elias Okafor’s goal with an xG of 0.994 [#905, #975].
- Seabrook Town scored 4 goals with expected goals totalling 3.87, significantly higher than Harbour City’s 1.82 xG [final_score, goals, team_stats].
- Kian Romano scored two late goals at 90+2' and 90+3' with high xGs of 0.745 and 0.956 respectively, completing the comeback [#1882, #1906].
- Joon Whitfield from Seabrook Town received a red card at 43' but the team still managed to win [#870, #871].

- Seabrook Town's comeback and late goals were facilitated by their strategy shift at 65', where, while trailing, they increased their pressing intensity (press from 0.66 to 0.84), raised their defensive line height (from 0.6 to 0.72), and played more direct (directness from 0.42 to 0.57). This tactical adjustment aimed to regain possession higher up and quickly exploit chances, consistent with their 3-4-3 formation favoring wide crossing play by quickly advancing the ball forward [1361].

- The goal at 53' by Tariq Marlowe came from a regain of possession followed by an immediate shot without passes, showing Seabrook Town's ability to win the ball high and strike swiftly, reflecting their pressing and direct approach post-tactical change [1103,1104].

- Seabrook Town's winning goals late in the match (90+2', 90+3') show effective counter-attacking patterns, with quick regains and short passing moves leading to goals. For example, Kian Romano's goal at 90+2' stemmed from a two-pass sequence after ball recovery, supported by a through assist, indicating their 3-4-3 shape enabled rapid transition exploiting space [1881,1882]. The next goal also involved a short passing buildup, reflecting structured but swift wide play and penetration [1905,1906].

- Harbour City operated a 4-2-3-1 with a patient short passing style aiming to build long possession phases, exemplified by their first goal buildup with 17 passes over 57 seconds starting from open play, showcasing their attempt to control tempo and create chances patiently [904,905]. Their goal at 47' came from a corner and a quick cross, fitting their style of mix of patient buildup but capitalizing on set-piece opportunities [973,975].

- The higher ppda (pressing aggression) of Seabrook Town overall (6.8 vs Harbour City's 9.1) and higher possession and field tilt reflect their controlling style after tactical changes, while Harbour City faced more turnovers especially in the second half (7 vs 14), indicating difficulty in retaining ball under the opposing pressing pressure [team_stats].

- The red card at 43' to Joon Whitfield (Seabrook Town) likely forced tactical adaptations, possibly influencing their initial subdued pressing and patient buildup in the first half but prompted more aggressive pressing in the second half as they chased the game [870,871,1361].
